understanding the mechanisms by which adipose tissue regulates cardiovascular risk in obesity and how these mechanisms can be manipulated to prevent the development of obesity related metabolic diseases.

the COX and DDDAH enzymes are important regulators of adipose tissue metabolism and that their modulation may have therapeutic potential for the treatment of obesity and obesity related metabolic diseases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity is associated with the release of two important cardiovascular risk factors from adipose tissue; IL-6 and ADMA.
the COX pathway and DDAH in adipose tissue may have a significant role in regulating the development of obesity associated metabolic disease.
adipose tissue is a major source of circulating ADMA and IL-6 and these factors may contribute to the development of metabolic disease.
The main takeaway from our work is that
adipose tissue is an active metabolic organ with a role in the development of obesity associated disease.
adipose tissue is a major source of ADMA and IL-6, which may underlie the development of obesity-associated metabolic disease.
adipose tissue is not just a passive storage depot for energy but a dynamic organ that can actively release factors that may contribute to metabolic disease.
